summary.name: Cursor
summary.one_liner: Cursor is an AI coding agent and IDE that turns development tasks into code, with agents that can work autonomously, in parallel, and across terminal, Slack, and GitHub.
keywords: hand off coding tasks to ai
use_cases: Handing off coding tasks to an AI agent
Building features end to end with autonomous agents
Reviewing pull requests in GitHub with AI
Coding from the terminal with AI assistance
Using AI bots in Slack for team development work
Running multiple coding agents in parallel
summary.what_it_does: Cursor is presented as a coding agent for building software. Agents turn ideas or handed-off tasks into code, and they can use their own computers to build, test, and demo features for review. Cursor runs in the terminal via a CLI installed with a curl command, integrates with Slack, and reviews pull requests in GitHub. Users can choose among models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Cursor, and launch fleets of agents that work in parallel for hours or days. The page also mentions an Agent SDK and AI bots that can sign in to tools and return finished work.
notable: Agents use their own computers to build, test, and demo features end to end
Choice of models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Cursor's own
Parallel agent fleets that can run for hours or days
Integrations with terminal, Slack, and GitHub PR reviews
caveats: Page is mostly marketing; no pricing tiers or plan details are shown on the page
Platform support beyond the named integrations is not detailed on the page
Listing describes it as using GPT-4, but the page itself does not name GPT-4
